text: The five operations whose owner in Microservice Ownership Map v1 is PLT (the four feature-flag paths and POST /admin/workflows/smoke) are published in gateway-bff.yaml, the edge document of the set, with their v4 paths unchanged and no new base path.
why: R8.4 splits the API Specification into 19 service documents plus gateway-bff and an index; PLT is a platform library and not one of the 19 services, so no service document may hold these operations and no source gives a platform base path.
read: The five operations stay one contract surface at the edge; rwb-reporting, rwb-case and the other services do not repeat them. The base path under the BFF is not stated anywhere, so the operations are read as reachable on the edge route /api/recovery of the gateway-bff.
applied_in: gateway-bff.yaml (5 operations: GET /feature-flags, GET /admin/feature-flags, POST /admin/feature-flags, PATCH /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}, POST /admin/workflows/smoke); index.yaml x-document-set row PLT
impact: If the platform library gets its own contract document, five operations and one index row move; the 19 service documents and their 136 operations are unaffected.

text: The composite screen routes of gateway-bff (DP-19) are not written into the v5 document set; they are left to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the gateway-bff document records the edge rules (one hop, session in Redis, 2 s budget) instead of a route contract.
why: No source gives a composite path, operation, parameter or response, and rule 8 of the run forbids inventing a value; R8.4 asks for a gateway-bff file but not for a route contract that does not exist.
read: Every document of the set is a service or edge contract with the operations of v4 only; a screen composes them at the BFF and the contract of that composition is a story output of RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
applied_in: gateway-bff.yaml info.description (edge rules paragraph) and servers; index.yaml x-document-set row PLT
impact: A developer reading the edge document finds no screen route; the composite route is designed and published later under RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

text: Each event payload field named in Event and Messaging Design v4 is carried into the AsyncAPI 3.0 documents as a JSON property name with no type, no format and no required flag; the missing types are recorded in CG-B-ARCH-API-3 rather than guessed.
why: The Payload column gives field names only, and the Arch v5 event catalogue gives no schema; rule 8 of the run forbids inventing a value, and a guessed type would become a contract that no source supports.
read: The property names, the event name (rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1), the topic, the producer and the consumers are contract; the type of each field is open until the registry schema exists.
applied_in: asyncapi/*.asyncapi.yaml components.schemas.<Event>Event data properties; info.description of each AsyncAPI document
impact: A consumer cannot generate a typed client from the AsyncAPI document until the JSON Schema of each payload is published; the field names, topics, keys and envelope are fixed.

text: The rwb-reporting AsyncAPI document declares the topic rwb.reporting.events.v1 with no channel, and the guarantee-claim events are carried as one message named GuaranteeClaim on rwb.guarantee.events.v1 (topic by the R4 naming rule) with TreatmentClosed on rwb.treatment.events.v1.
why: No event is catalogued for rwb-reporting, and the slide 43 carry-on row gives a dash topic and the wildcard name GuaranteeClaim*; the R4 naming rule fixes the topic of a service as rwb.<short>.events.v1, which is the only source for the missing topic cell.
read: rwb-reporting consumes the events of the other services and publishes none in this release; rwb-guarantee publishes one message whose exact event names are still open.
applied_in: asyncapi/rwb-reporting.asyncapi.yaml (channels {} and x-note); asyncapi/rwb-guarantee.asyncapi.yaml; asyncapi/rwb-treatment.asyncapi.yaml; index.yaml x-asyncapi-documents
impact: If rwb-reporting publishes an event later, or the guarantee events are split by claim type, the two AsyncAPI documents are reissued; no REST operation changes.

text: The seven component schemas that no operation references are kept, each in the document of the service that owns its domain: DocumentVersion, FieldCaptureItem and FieldCaptureManifest in rwb-document.yaml, Listing in rwb-asset.yaml, PlacementResult and QueueOwnerLoad in rwb-case.yaml, WriteOff in rwb-writeoff.yaml.
why: Rule 1 and the work package keep every section of the source, so the schemas may not be dropped; the split by owner needs one home for each, and the domain of the name decides it.
read: The seven schemas are definitions only and are reachable from no path of the set; the three documents that hold them stay valid OpenAPI documents.
applied_in: rwb-document.yaml, rwb-asset.yaml, rwb-case.yaml and rwb-writeoff.yaml components.schemas; index.yaml x-unreferenced-schemas
impact: A registry publish of the set would carry seven unused schemas until they are retired or an operation is named for them.

text: The shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 has one AsyncAPI document (asyncapi/rwb.decision-record.v1.asyncapi.yaml) that covers all 19 producers, and every service document names it under x-shared-topics instead of repeating the channel.
why: Arch v5 slide 42 gives the topic one producer cell, 'all 19', and DP-03 makes every service write DecisionRecorded; 19 copies of the same channel contract would drift and no source asks for the repetition.
read: DecisionRecorded has one contract, produced by every service and consumed by rwb-decision and rwb-reporting; the 19 service documents remain complete for their own topics.
applied_in: asyncapi/rwb.decision-record.v1.asyncapi.yaml; x-shared-topics in the 19 service AsyncAPI documents; index.yaml x-asyncapi-documents
impact: A tool that reads one service document only sees the shared topic by reference, not inline.

text: The two header lines of Template and Rules R8.1 are the first two lines of every YAML file of the set, written as YAML comments, followed by the change-log comment row of 5.0.0.
why: R8.1 requires the two lines at the start of every new document, and a YAML document cannot start with two bare prose lines without ceasing to be valid YAML; a comment keeps both the requirement and the parse.
read: The first two lines read '# SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 22 November 2026.' and '# (C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd', and the fifth line carries '5.0.0, 22 November 2026, D-RCV-60 microservice realignment, T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash'.
applied_in: All 21 OpenAPI documents and all 20 AsyncAPI documents of the set
impact: A checker that reads the header without stripping the comment marker sees a leading '# '; no content line is affected.

text: The v4 info.description (the full version history and scope note) is kept once, in index.yaml; each service document carries a scoped description that names its operations, its base, its schema, its topic and the operations moved in or out.
why: Keeping a 4,000-character module description in 21 documents would repeat it without adding contract meaning, while dropping it entirely would lose a section of the source.
read: Every number, date and paragraph of the v4 description is still in the set, in the index; a service document describes its own surface and points to the index.
applied_in: index.yaml info.description; info.description of the 19 service documents and of gateway-bff.yaml
impact: A reader who opens only one service document does not see the v4 version history; the pointer to index.yaml is in its description.

text: Every operation of the set carries x-owner with the owner code of Microservice Ownership Map v1, and the 20 operations whose owner differs from the v4 x-module also carry x-owner-note with the v4 module and the assumption that moves the owner.
why: The split by owner must be checkable in the document itself, and the reader of a moved operation has to see why it sits in a document whose module differs from its x-module.
read: x-module is kept exactly as v4 wrote it; x-owner is the realigned owner; the pair differs on exactly the 20 operations listed in index.yaml x-owner-changes.
applied_in: 141 operations across the 20 OpenAPI documents; index.yaml x-owner-changes (20 rows)
impact: A tool that reads x-module as the owner sees the v4 module, not the service; x-owner is the field to read.

text: API Specification v5 is issued in Draft status with no approval recorded, as the next version of the v4 family in the folder 'Recovery Workbench API Specification v5'.
why: This run is the D-RCV-60 realignment: no human approval step is available and the run must not stop for one, so the missing approval and status are recorded as an assumption.
read: The document set is complete as a split of v4 and may be cited by the architecture, contract and story documents of this run; the approval is recorded afterwards by the owner of the API specification.
applied_in: info.version 5.0.0 of every document; index.yaml x-decision and x-change-log
impact: A contract that is cited before approval carries Draft status; the operation, schema and owner content is unaffected.
